newsitem.title: USA: Unicom unit named in Sears Tower complaint.
newsitem.headline: Unicom unit named in Sears Tower complaint.

text.p: The operator of the Sears Tower and an Illinois energy company on Monday said they filed a complaint with the Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC), seeking to force Commonwealth Edison to allow an electric cogeneration system to be installed in the Chicago building.

Tower Leasing Inc, which operates the tallest building in North America, and QST, a unit of CILCORP Inc, said the utility refused to connect with the proposed cogeneration system. Commonwealth Edison is a unit of Unicom Corp.
The companies said the cogeneration system could provide $2.0 million in annual energy savings.

John Buck Co, Tower Leasing's property management firm, is working with QST to install a cogeneration system utilizing engine-driven generators to supply electricity during peak-use periods, the companies said.

In a statement, Commonwealth Edison criticized the Sears Tower proposal, claiming the plan could deny the building's 100 tenants with the expected benefits of a deregulated energy market. Deregulation would allow users to buy electricity from a variety of suppliers.
The utility also said it cannot "safely" connect with the cogeneration system.

"As it is currently configured, our distribution network in the tower cannot be safely connected to QST's proposed cogeneration system," Bill Downey, vice president of customer operations at Commonwealth Edison, said in a statement.

Commonwealth Edison also said that, in order for the estimated $10 million cogeneration system to work, QST would need to purchase the utility's existing distribution system in the building. The utility said it was under no obligation to sell that network to QST.
Tower Leasing and QST, in their complaint to the commission, allege that Commonwealth Edison's refusal to provide a connection with the cogeneration system violates the Illinois Public Utilities Act.
